name: wan-s1-bulk
description: Plan 11.3's bulk half on the S1 production profile, over a real path: 60 s of iperf3 each way, three repetitions, all four pairs interleaved (GG, RR, GR, RG) so the path's own variation hits Go and Rust equally. The path is chosen on the command line (`--server-host`/`--server-addr`), because one scenario serves every rung of the RTT ladder in tools/lab/README.md. The iperf3 bitrate cap (400 Mbit/s) is a guard rail, not the measurement: it is well above what a 1-vCPU box drives through a tunnel at this RTT, so it does not bind, but it stops an unexpectedly fast path from saturating lab-arm64's NIC (tools/lab/README.md, safety rule 6). A cap that binds makes every implementation report the cap, which is how the first attempt at this rung wasted half an hour: 60 Mbit/s, 60 Mbit/s, both directions, both implementations. Ports: the tunnel is 29910+ and the pingpong target 22700, not the 29900/22600 defaults, so a WAN run cannot collide with a netns lab that is up on either host, the port check unions the host's listeners with both lab namespaces', and a detached soak owns the defaults inside kr-srv. Measured on the 131 ms rung before the campaign: a Go client on one vCPU drove 200 Mbit/s up (cap-bound) and 145 Mbit/s down at a load average of 0.93, so the real limit is the client's single core, not the path, the cap is set above that so it never becomes the thing being compared. The reverse test starts 95 s after the forward one, not 70: one `iperf3 -s` serves both, and at 131 ms a finished forward test is still draining the tunnel's smux buffers when the next one dials, which is exactly how the first S2 session lost its last three runs to `the server is busy running a test`. The 400 Mbit/s cap in this file is the one that fits the 131 ms rung it was written for; on the 95.3 ms rung a Go client alone drives 631 Mbit/s, so it BINDS there. The cap belongs to the path, so pass `--bitrate` per session (11.3b ran at 900M) rather than editing this file, and check the workload command line printed beside each result.
